blocker_results.question: What official normative evidence determines the resulting .u32 value of base scalar add.u32 when the mathematical sum is outside the unsigned 32-bit range?
blocker_results.rationale: Searches of the official PTX ISA 9.3 HTML found no explicit normative rule (and no combination of explicit normative fragments without an unsupported assumption) that determines the resulting .u32 value when the mathematical sum of the two .u32 source values is outside the unsigned 32-bit range. Terms such as 'wraparound' (0 matches) and 'modulo' (0 matches) do not occur. The 'truncated' matches found are scoped to other instructions (redux.sync .add reduction operation; ld/st/cvt operand-size rules in section 9.4.1), the 'overflow' matches are saturating-modifier notes for saturating forms and bfe/shlf-internal variables, and the 'carry' matches concern only the extended-precision instructions of section 9.7.2. Section 9.6 states that instruction semantics are described using C, which frames how the add Semantics block 'd = a + b;' is written but does not import an explicit overflow/result-width rule into the PTX normative text. The two fragments above are the closest searched official context and are recorded for traceability; they do not resolve the blocker.

blocker_results.question: What official normative evidence determines the machine-state effect when an instruction's complete optional guard expression evaluates false?
blocker_results.rationale: Explicit normative fragments establish that the guard predicate 'controls conditional execution of the instruction' (sections 9.3 and 4.3.2), that instructions without a guard are 'executed unconditionally' (section 9.3), and the official examples show a guarded add executes the add when the guard is true and show a false @!p guard prevents a branch instruction's branch action ('if False, branch over'). These fragments partially support the proposition that a false complete guard expression prevents instruction execution. No explicit clause was found stating the resulting machine-state effect (for example, that the entire state is unchanged) when a value-writing instruction such as add.u32 has a false guard. The blocker is therefore only partially supported.

This frames how the add Semantics block 'd = a + b;' is to be read, but it does not state any overflow, truncation, or result-width rule for base add.u32; recorded so the searched context is traceable.

fragments.exact_quote: Instructions add.cc, addc, sub.cc, subc, mad.cc and madc reference an implicitly specified condition code register (CC) having a single carry flag bit (CC.CF) holding carry-in/carry-out or borrow-in/borrow-out. These instructions support extended-precision integer addition, subtraction, and multiplication. No other instructions access the condition code, and there is no support for setting, clearing, or testing the condition code. The condition code register is not preserved across calls and is mainly intended for use in straight-line code sequences for computing extended-precision integer addition, subtraction, and multiplication.

fragments.context_after: 10061-10066: 'The extended-precision arithmetic instructions are:' followed by list items add.cc/addc, sub.cc/subc, mad.cc/madc
fragments.reason_for_inclusion: Neighboring normative context for BLOCK-1: enumerates the only instructions that access the condition code carry flag and states that no other instructions access it, so base add is not among the instructions that record carry-out; the section does not state how base add computes its result when the mathematical sum exceeds the 32-bit range. Recorded so the searched carry/overflow context is traceable.

fragments.exact_quote: All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.
fragments.context_before: 7541-7546: predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier; declaration .reg .pred p, q, r;
fragments.context_after: 7551-7552: Predicates are most commonly set as the result of a comparison performed by the setp instruction.
fragments.reason_for_inclusion: Primary normative guard rule for BLOCK-2: the guard predicate 'controls conditional execution of the instruction' and instructions without a guard are 'executed unconditionally'. This is the closest official statement connecting the complete guard expression to whether execution occurs; it does not explicitly state the machine-state effect when the guard evaluates false.

fragments.exact_quote: Instructions are formed from an instruction opcode followed by a comma-separated list of zero or more operands, and terminated with a semicolon. Operands may be register variables, constant expressions, address expressions, or label names. Instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution. The guard predicate follows the optional label and precedes the opcode, and is written as @p, where p is a predicate register. The guard predicate may be optionally negated, written as @!p.

fragments.reason_for_inclusion: Shared guard-syntax rule for BLOCK-2: corroborates section 9.3 by stating that instructions have an optional guard predicate which 'controls conditional execution', written @p or @!p. It does not state the machine-state effect when the complete guard expression evaluates false.

remaining_evidence_gaps.description: No official PTX ISA 9.3 normative rule was found that determines the resulting .u32 value of base scalar add.u32 when the mathematical sum is outside the unsigned 32-bit range (overflow/result-width treatment).

No explicit official clause states the machine-state effect when an instruction's complete guard expression evaluates false; existing evidence partially supports that a false guard prevents instruction execution but does not state the resulting state (e.g., that all state is unchanged).

curation_notes: This supplementary evidence artifact is evidence-only and covers exactly the two blocking issues BLOCK-1 and BLOCK-2 of the blocked semantic interpretation ptx-9.3-add-u32-semantics-v1. It does not replace the primary source bundle ptx-9.3-add-u32-source-bundle-v1.

Only the official NVIDIA PTX ISA 9.3 HTML (documents/sources/nvidia/ptx/9.3/raw/ptx_isa_9.3.html, SHA-256 e2095c4ae00fe81fa18325b8e26c4a41b94965295c7affd7ff7f787fd98a8856) was searched, using the restricted specification tools (spec_search, spec_get_context, spec_read_span). No CUDA C, compiler behavior, another ISA, or unofficial sources were used as evidence. In particular, section 9.6's statement that semantics are 'described using C' is recorded as context only; no C-language overflow semantics were imported as evidence.

BLOCK-1 classification NOT_FOUND: the searched official HTML contains no explicit overflow/result-width rule for base add.u32 and no combination of the found fragments establishes the result without an unsupported assumption. This is not a semantic interpretation; it is a statement about the absence of resolving evidence.

BLOCK-2 classification PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED: fragments PTX-9.3-ADD-SUP-003 through PTX-9.3-ADD-SUP-006 provide explicit official evidence that the guard controls conditional execution and that a false @!p guard prevents a branch instruction's action, but no explicit clause states the machine-state effect of a false guard on a value-writing instruction such as add.u32.
